title: Basilicata's Metano Prices Have Nearly Doubled the National Climb Since Tracking Began
dek: A quiet day at the pump masks a nine-week story: Benzina and Gasolio in Basilicata mostly tracked Italy's overall drift, but Metano surged 38.5% versus the nation's 17.7%, while GPL alone got cheaper even as it rose nationally.
executive_summary: On September 21, 2026, self-service fuel in Basilicata held almost perfectly flat against the day before. Benzina ticked up a fraction of a cent to €2.1771/L (+0.01%), Gasolio rose slightly more to €2.3555/L (+0.10%), while GPL and Metano didn't move at all, holding at €0.7857/L and €1.939/L respectively. Compared with the national self-service averages for the same day, Basilicata sits close to the Italian mean on Benzina (0.56% above) and Gasolio (0.19% below), but notably apart on the two gaseous fuels: GPL runs about 3.96% above the national price and Metano roughly 8.82% above it. Of the region's 270 registered stations, 241 reported prices today — an 89.3% reporting rate, slightly below the national 90.2%.

The day-to-day snapshot undersells what's actually happened this quarter. Looking at the weekly averages tracked since late July (week of 2026-07-20 through week of 2026-09-14), Benzina and Gasolio in Basilicata moved roughly in step with the rest of the country — Benzina up 8.6% regionally versus 8.7% nationally, Gasolio up 5.3% regionally versus 5.8% nationally. The real divergence is in the gaseous fuels. GPL in Basilicata actually fell 3.5% over those nine tracked weeks even as the national GPL average barely moved (down 0.5%), while Metano did the opposite: it climbed 38.5% regionally, more than double the 17.7% national increase — though much of that regional swing likely reflects a small, thinly-reported local Metano market, and the region's Metano price has in fact held flat at €1.939/L since September 14.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina Nudges Higher, Basilicata Tracks the National Curve Almost Exactly
paragraphs: Basilicata's self-service Benzina price edged up to €2.1771/L on September 21, a gain of just €0.0002 (+0.01%) from the previous day's €2.1769/L — effectively unchanged. That puts the region 0.56% above the national self-service average of €2.1650/L. Served-price Benzina in Basilicata sat at €2.2896/L, unchanged from the day before.

Zooming out to the nine tracked weeks (week of 2026-07-20 through week of 2026-09-14), Basilicata's Benzina rose from a weekly average of €1.9866/L to €2.1574/L, an increase of 8.6%. Nationally, the same period saw Benzina climb from €1.9756/L to €2.1479/L, up 8.7%. The two lines are essentially moving together — Basilicata just runs a hair above the national average throughout, and the acceleration visible in early-to-mid September shows up in both the region and the country as a whole, suggesting this is a nationwide cost pressure rather than anything Basilicata-specific.

fuel_sections.heading: Gasolio Climbs Faster Than Benzina, But Basilicata Is Actually a Touch Cheaper Than the National Average
paragraphs: Gasolio self-service in Basilicata rose to €2.3555/L on September 21, up €0.0024 (+0.10%) from €2.3531/L the day before. Unlike Benzina, Basilicata's Gasolio price sits slightly below the national self-service average of €2.3601/L — about 0.19% cheaper. Served-price Gasolio reached €2.4854/L, up from €2.4833/L.

Over the nine tracked weeks, Basilicata's Gasolio weekly average rose from €2.1793/L to €2.2945/L, a 5.3% increase. Nationally, Gasolio climbed from €2.1747/L to €2.3004/L, up 5.8% — a slightly steeper national rise than what Basilicata experienced. The gap is modest, but it's consistent: Basilicata's Gasolio has run at or just under the national average across nearly every tracked week, and the pattern held even as prices accelerated through September.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL Is the Outlier — Basilicata's Price Has Actually Fallen While the Rest of Italy Held Steady
paragraphs: GPL in Basilicata was unchanged on September 21, holding at €0.7857/L for self-service, the same as the day before — it has been stuck at this exact figure since September 12. That price is still meaningfully above the national self-service average of €0.7558/L, a premium of roughly 3.96%. Served-price GPL, in contrast, sat at €0.7565/L, essentially matching the national served average of €0.7566/L.

This is the clearest divergence of the two mid-sized fuels: across the nine tracked weeks, Basilicata's GPL weekly average actually dropped from €0.8140/L to €0.7857/L, a decline of 3.5%, while the national GPL average was nearly flat, down just 0.5% (from €0.7592/L to €0.7554/L). Basilicata's GPL price ran consistently above the national figure through the summer, then converged sharply in the weeks of September 7 and September 14 as the regional price fell while the national price held — the gap has visibly narrowed even if it hasn't closed.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano Is the Story of the Quarter: Basilicata's Price Has Outrun the National Climb by More Than Two to One
paragraphs: Metano in Basilicata held at €1.939/L for self-service on September 21, flat versus the day before and flat for the past week. That price runs 8.82% above the national self-service average of €1.7819/L, the widest regional-to-national gap of any of the four fuels tracked today. Served-price Metano was €1.812/L, also unchanged from the previous day.

The multi-week trend is the single most notable number in this report: Basilicata's weekly Metano average climbed from €1.40/L in the week of July 20 to €1.939/L in the week of September 14 — a 38.5% increase — while the national Metano average rose from €1.4999/L to €1.7653/L over the same span, up 17.7%. Basilicata's Metano price has grown more than twice as fast as the national rate. Some of that regional swing likely reflects Basilicata's small Metano-selling station count, where price changes at just a few pumps move the regional average more sharply than they would nationally; it's also worth noting the region's price has been flat at €1.939/L since September 14, suggesting the run-up has paused for now rather than continuing to accelerate.

network_section.heading: 241 of 270 Stations Reporting — A Rate Just Under the National Norm
paragraphs: Basilicata has 270 registered fuel stations in the MIMIT registry, of which 241 reported prices on September 21 — an 89.3% reporting rate. That's a touch below the national reporting rate of 90.2% (21,658 of 24,002 registered stations reporting), though the gap is small enough to fall within normal day-to-day variation rather than signaling a reporting problem specific to the region.

A sub-90% reporting rate, regionally and nationally, means roughly one in ten registered stations isn't submitting same-day prices — most commonly because a station is temporarily closed, mid-changeover, or simply late to file that day's figures with MIMIT. For a smaller region like Basilicata with only 270 stations total, each non-reporting station has a proportionally bigger effect on how representative the regional average is, which is part of why fuels with fewer active sellers — like Metano and GPL — show sharper local price swings than Benzina or Gasolio.

methodology_section.heading: How This Report Gets Made: No Analyst, No Spreadsheet, Just an Automated Pipeline
paragraphs: Everything in this report — pulling the day's price data from Italy's MIMIT registry, selecting today's featured region on a fixed alphabetical rotation, computing the weekly regional-versus-national trends, and writing the analysis above — runs automatically every day with no person in the loop. The pipeline is built with Claude Code, Anthropic's coding agent: it ingests the source data, aggregates it into the daily and weekly figures shown throughout this report, and an AI agent reads those figures fresh each morning and writes a new analysis grounded in that day's actual numbers.

The alternative — and the way most fuel-price tracking still gets done — is a manually maintained spreadsheet: someone downloads a CSV, pastes it into Excel, updates a chart, and writes a summary by hand, typically on whatever cadence that person has time for. This pipeline replaces that entire manual loop with unattended, same-day, region-by-region reporting across all 20 Italian regions in rotation, at a consistency and speed a manual process can't match.

closing.heading: Explore Beyond Basilicata

pull_quote: Basilicata's Metano price has climbed 38.5% since late July — more than double Italy's 17.7% national rise over the same nine weeks.
caption:
Today's regional spotlight on Fuel Dashboard: Basilicata. The stand-out number isn't at the pump today — Benzina and Gasolio barely moved — it's in the nine weeks of history behind it. Basilicata's Metano price has climbed 38.5% since late July, more than double Italy's 17.7% national increase over the same period. GPL tells the opposite story: it's actually down 3.5% regionally while the national price barely moved.

Fuel Dashboard is a free, interactive tracker of Italian fuel prices — Benzina, Gasolio, GPL and Metano — broken down by Region, Province, Municipality and Operator/Brand, updated daily from Italy's official MIMIT registry. Today's report, including the full weekly regional-vs-national breakdown for all four fuels, is live now at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/.

Here's what I think is the more interesting part: nothing about today's report was built by hand. The data pull, the region rotation, the weekly trend analysis, even this caption — all generated automatically every day by a pipeline I built with Claude Code. No spreadsheet, no manual chart update, no person deciding what to write that morning. It's a live case study in using AI coding tools to replace a manual Excel workflow with something that just runs itself, every single day, at a level of consistency a person doing this by hand couldn't sustain.

If you're curious what a fully automated, self-updating data project looks like end to end, take a look.
